[MUQATIL:74:18-30/r6] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Al-Walid turned away arrogantly and called the Qur'an transmitted magic and human speech.
[TAB-FULL:v23p432/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | He turned away from faith and belief in God's revelation, arrogantly refusing the truth; he claimed the Qur'an was magic taken from another person.
[NAHHAS:v5p67/r6] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | He turned away from truth and arrogantly refused belief after preparing to refute the signs, although he did not disdain bowing to powerless stones.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r2] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · السدي وتوبة | reports | Al-Suddi glosses busur as changed; the line attributed to Tuba illustrates the term for altered, rejecting manner.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r3] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | holds | Al-Mawardi suggests al-Walid may have frowned and scowled at the Prophet when the Prophet called him.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r4] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | holds | Alternatively, he may have scowled at those who believed in and supported the Prophet.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r5] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | holds | The text distinguishes scowling that appears after conversation from scowling that appears before it.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r6] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | One explanation is that he turned away from the truth and became arrogant toward obedience.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r7] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | Another explanation is that he physically left his place and spoke arrogantly.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | He turned away toward his family as a denier.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | He arrogantly held himself above accepting faith.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p430/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · مقاتل | reports | Muqatil says he turned away from faith and grew arrogant when invited to it.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:21-27/r3] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | He turned away and grew arrogant toward faith.
[JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | reports | The passage is said to concern al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi, wealthy with sons and called al-Wahid among his people, according to Ibn Amir.
[JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | reports | In the story, al-Walid rejects calling Muhammad a soothsayer, poet, or madman, then chooses “magician” and says the Qur’an separates families.
[JISHUMI:v10p7156/r9] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Idbār means turning rearward, opposite turning forward; tadabbur considers an outcome.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p269/r7] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | He turned away from faith and became arrogant when invited to it.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r14] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | He turned away from the truth and arrogantly rejected it before making his accusation.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | reports | If the curse praises his first judgment, al-Walid reconsidered the Quran, saw Muhammad's superior rank, frowned from envy, then turned away in pride and called it magic.
[TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r24] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | He turned away from faith and acted arrogantly when called to it.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | He turned away from faith and acted arrogantly when called to it.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p178/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | He turned away from the rest of the people toward his family, and arrogantly refused to believe.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p178/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The fāʾ marks immediate sequence: after turning away in pride, he voiced this objection.
[QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r6] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Al-Walid turned away and went to his family.
[QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | He was too arrogant to believe.
[QURTUBI-FULL:74:23-25/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · قوم | reports | Another view says he turned away from faith and became arrogant when invited to it.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:74:20-28/r5] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | He turned away from the truth or the Messenger and arrogantly refused to follow.
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#12/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | He turned away from the truth.
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#12/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | He arrogantly rejected the truth, or acted proudly regarding his own status and speech.
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#12/r3] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | “Then he looked” is coordinated with “he thought and plotted”; the curse is parenthetical, and repeated thumma marks the delay between actions.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · غير مسمى | reports | The frowning and scowling may show al-Walīd's options had run out, or describe his expression toward the Prophet; turning away can be physical or a departure from truth, and arrogance may mean haughtiness toward truth.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Abū Ḥayyān treats these gestures as satirical signs of fabrication: a truthful judgment would bring visible joy and need no strained, delayed deliberation; another view says he considered the Qurʾān's proofs before frowning.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The conjunctions distinguish related acts: frowning and scowling are near-synonyms, arrogance causes turning away, while the fāʾ signals his immediate utterance after forming the charge.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r6] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Al-Walid turned from truth and retreated arrogantly, refusing to submit to the Quran.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r9] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The man is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi, a Quraysh leader.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r7] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Although reflection led him toward faith in the Qur’an’s soundness, he turned away from that conclusion and proudly refused to acknowledge the truth.
[BIQAI-FULL:v8p227/r8] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | His conceit was extreme: he brought himself to reject the truth even though he was in great need of acknowledging it.
[BURSEVI:v10p178/r1] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | He turned from truth, arrogantly refused to follow it, and then spoke.
[ALUSI-FULL:v29p124#4/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | He turned away from the truth—or from the Messenger—and arrogantly refused to follow him.
[ELMALILI:74:14-25/r17] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | He turned from the truth, turned his back on faith toward unbelief, and arrogantly refused to acknowledge the truth.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The successive actions coordinate with “devised”; the sequence is a rise in rank, not time, because all occurred during his thinking and planning.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r5] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | One possible metaphor is that he abandoned his effort to devise a description for the Qur’an in despair, then turned to arrogant disdain. | mentions 74:18
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r6] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Alternatively, “turned away” may mean that he increasingly rejected belief in the Prophet, as Pharaoh is described turning away. | mentions 79:22
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p309#2/r7] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The successive expressions satirically portray al-Walīd’s contortions as he strained to invent a description for the Qur’an.
[TABATABAI:74:12-25/r10] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The sequence portrays al-Walid after deliberation: he looks to judge, frowns and shows disgust, then turns away and grows arrogant before speaking.
[TABATABAI:74:12-25/r13] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Turning away and pride are inner states sequenced after visible facial states because they become evident in his words; fa links his words to those attitudes, not thumma.
[ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n11/r1] ASAD-NOTES, d. 1412 · author | holds | Asad directs readers to 96:6-7 for comparison. | mentions 96:6, 96:7
[ASAD-NOTES:74:16/r3] ASAD-NOTES, d. 1412 · author | holds | On hearing the messages, he reflects on how to disprove them, destroys himself by that deliberation, looks for arguments, frowns, then turns away and glories in arrogance.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r2] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | The arrogant Quraysh leader fashioned a disdainfully delivered excuse, misjudging the Qur’an as a prophet’s stirring eloquence and ignoring its warning, though its statements are realities he will soon meet.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p45/r3] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | The Qur'an depicts his arrogance: he assesses listeners' moods, frowns to signal a hopeless judgment, then turns away muttering.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r3] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | Verses 18–25 condemn people who, like al-Walīd, adopt a similar unbelieving posture toward the Qur’an.
[STUDYQURAN:74:11/r23] STUDYQURAN · Ṭ | reports | Turning his back means al-Walīd rejected faith and affirming the Quran.
[STUDYQURAN:74:11/r24] STUDYQURAN · Ṭ, JJ | reports | Istakbara is read with an implied ʿan (“from”), so it means he disdained to affirm the truth or scorned the Prophet.
